_: V90Mapper's constructor is eleven stores, a 0x50-byte allocation and a
six-word loop; its destructor is one guarded free.  Every mutation here
is meant to be caught by t_v90modchain's whole-object comparison over
never-zeroed storage, by its absolute allocation accounting, or by the
free/free_null split that makes the null guard testable.
THE FIELD NAMES CHANGED WHEN THE TWO RESETS WERE WRITTEN.  cleared_004,
cleared_00c, cleared_010, cleared_014, cleared_658, cleared_6f8 and
cleared_6fc are now bitsPerFrame, signBitsPerFrame, signBitGroups,
signBitGroupSize, constellationSize, uint_6f8 and signEncoder.prev_;
the anchors below were rewritten with them.  A find string that no
longer matches is an UNUSABLE mutation and does NOT fail a run
(finding F347), so `make phase`'s anchor check is what caught this.
ANCHORING IN THE RESETS NEEDS EXTRA CONTEXT.  The two functions share a
long identical run -- the six-constellation fill and the seven-word
modulusEncoder fill are written out twice -- so a find string taken from
inside it matches twice and is rejected as NOT UNIQUE.  Each anchor
below therefore reaches back to the nearest line that differs.

_: The law arms, mutated in `reset`'s copy: the anchor reaches forward to
the spectral-shaper branch, which only `reset` has.  Mutating the pair
in resetNoSpectral's copy would be the same three verdicts over the
same fill loop, so it is done once.
ONE CONVERSION CANNOT BE MUTATED HERE.  Dropping the (unsigned char)
cast from `~(b & 0x7f)` is NOT caught, and that is a property of the
callee rather than a gap in the test: `ulaw2linear` takes an
`unsigned char`, so the int the mutation produces is truncated back to
the same eight bits at the call.  The cast is in the source because the
object's `not %al` is on the byte, not because anything can fail on it.
